title: Current Speaker of Parliament of Ghana: official-source research dataset

subject.party_affiliation_documented: National Democratic Congress (NDC), reported in the indexed text of Parliament's 2008 Nadowli West election-results PDF
subject.constituency_documented: Nadowli West, reported in indexed text for the 2008 election-results PDF
unresolved_profile_fields: Complete sequence of parliamentary terms and constituencies
Exact dates and portfolios for previous leadership and executive positions
Complete committee membership and chairmanship history
Direct contemporaneous Speaker-election ballot and vote total

coverage.scope_statement: Partial investigation of publicly accessible Parliament of Ghana pages and Parliament-hosted repositories; not an exhaustive crawl of the full site or all Hansards.

sources.title: Search results: order papers
sources.summary: Page showed selected 2016 order papers and one 2019 paper plus links to Office of the Speaker and parliamentary history.
sources.relevance: Initial discovery route requested in the research brief.
sources.notes: Selected results only; not a complete archive search.

sources.title: Office of the Speaker / Speakers of Parliament
sources.term_or_session: Fourth Republic; current at access date
sources.summary: Lists Bagbin as Speaker from 7 January 2021 ‘to date’; describes Speaker as presiding officer and Chairperson of Parliamentary Service Board.
sources.relevance: Primary identity and tenure verification.
sources.notes: Official rendering is Alban Kingsford Sumana Bagbin; no publication date shown.

sources.title: Parliament of Ghana homepage
sources.summary: Search index identifies Ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic and Bagbin as Speaker.
sources.relevance: Current office and term context.
sources.notes: Homepage not separately fetched; supported by SRC-002 and later dated news.

sources.title: Members of Parliament directory
sources.summary: Current directory has seven pages and lists current MP for Nadowli/Kaleo, not Bagbin.
sources.relevance: Coverage note: directory is current, not a historical member roster.
sources.notes: No historic Bagbin profile found on inspected listing; no page publication date shown.

sources.title: Legacy leadership listing route (unavailable)
sources.summary: Search index shows Bagbin as Speaker; direct requests returned 404.
sources.relevance: Preserves discovery failure; not substantive proof.
sources.notes: Do not rely on indexed listing in place of live page.

sources.title: Speeches of the Speaker — Rabat intervention
sources.summary: Lists Bagbin’s intervention at the Rabat meeting on 6 February 2025 and identifies him as Speaker and CoSPAL President.
sources.relevance: Public address and international parliamentary engagement.
sources.notes: Full speech text not exposed in fetched page; meeting date 2025-02-06.

sources.title: Communications from the Speaker — Appointments Committee
sources.summary: Lists formal communication concerning happenings at Appointments Committee on 31 January 2025.
sources.relevance: Official Speaker communication.
sources.notes: Full text not available from inspected representation; date refers to Appointments Committee event.

sources.title: Official Reports / Hansard archive
sources.summary: Initial page displayed 2026 daily Hansards and pages 1–42.
sources.relevance: Archive route for interventions and rulings.
sources.notes: Underlying daily Hansards not comprehensively searched.

sources.title: Order Paper archive
sources.summary: Initial page displayed recent 2026 order papers and addenda; pagination 1–27.
sources.relevance: Business archive coverage.
sources.notes: Not evidence of Bagbin participation without item-level review.

sources.title: Votes & Proceedings archive page reference
sources.summary: Search result showed 2025–2026 Votes and Proceedings; another surfaced page 50.
sources.relevance: Potential records lead.
sources.notes: Archive not processed sitting by sitting.

sources.title: Parliamentary Election Results for Upper West Region — 2008
sources.summary: Indexed document reports Bagbin (NDC), 12,997 votes (61.9%), in Nadowli West on election day 2008-12-07.
sources.relevance: Indexed electoral result relevant to his constituency and party history.
sources.notes: PDF identified but not fetched/text-processed; index renders name as Kinsford.

sources.title: Parliamentary Election Results — 2004
sources.summary: Repository item is titled Parliamentary Election Results - 2004 and links to 2004ParliamentaryResults.pdf.
sources.relevance: Potential source to resolve constituency and election history.
sources.notes: Repository item date says 2000; preserve conflict with title/file.

sources.title: 92 96 & 00 ELECTION RESULTS.xls
sources.summary: Parliament-hosted spreadsheet for 1992, 1996, 2000 results; Bagbin rows not extracted.
sources.relevance: Lead for early-election verification.
sources.notes: No Bagbin result inferred from preview; issue date not verified.

sources.title: Closing remarks at end of dissolution of Sixth Parliament
sources.summary: Repository identifies Bagbin as author/co-author; issue date January 2007; 2.95 MB PDF.
sources.relevance: Directly authored parliamentary speech record.
sources.notes: File not downloaded; duplicates older IR handle record.

sources.title: Formal Communication from the RT Hon Alban S.K. Bagbin, Speaker of Parliament
sources.locator: Repository item date and attached file listing
sources.summary: Author listed as S.K. Bagbin; Alban; issue date 2021-07-21; PDF 640.42 KB.
sources.relevance: Official communication by Bagbin as Speaker.
sources.notes: Repository access/ingest metadata dated 2026-07-07, separate from issue date; file text not processed.

sources.title: The Supreme Court in the life of the 1992 Constitution — taking stock and looking forward
sources.summary: Repository names Bagbin as author; alternative title calls it Speaker’s lecture for Supreme Court 150th anniversary; PDF 223.01 KB.
sources.relevance: Primary authored speech and constitutional/legal position.
sources.notes: PDF not locally processed; associated report SRC-021 is separate; lecture date 2026-07-23.

sources.title: Speaker rules on Minority motion as inadmissible
sources.summary: Parliament says Bagbin rejected a motion seeking an inquiry into narcotics seizures, citing Standing Orders and pending investigations/judicial proceedings; quotes ‘I accordingly dismiss this motion in limeine.’
sources.relevance: Explicit Speaker ruling and attributed reasons.
sources.notes: One caption typo says Bagbink; article otherwise uses Bagbin.

sources.title: Speaker justifies recall of Parliament
sources.summary: Indexed report says Bagbin justified the five-day emergency meeting ending 28 August 2026 and cited a presidential request dated 11 August.
sources.relevance: Speaker explanation of recall and business.
sources.notes: Full article not separately fetched.

sources.title: Decentralisation ensures oversight responsibilities
sources.summary: At Speaker’s Breakfast Forum, Bagbin linked decentralisation to legislative, administrative, oversight responsibilities and highlighted Parliament Television.
sources.relevance: Speaker policy remarks and institutional initiative.
sources.notes: Similar report CO=286 separately catalogued as SRC-020.

sources.title: Decentralisation ensures oversight responsibilities (duplicate report)
sources.summary: Search result describes the same decentralisation forum in substantially similar terms under another publication date.
sources.relevance: Separate official reporting of same event.
sources.notes: CO=284 states 7 March while this result says 4 March; discrepancy unresolved.

sources.title: Speaker Bagbin charges Supreme Court to deepen independence
sources.summary: Parliament summarizes lecture on Supreme Court constitutional role, rights, institutional overreach/restraint, and constitutional interpretation.
sources.relevance: Second official source representation of lecture SRC-016.
sources.notes: Same event as SRC-016, retained as separate source record; lecture date 2026-07-23.

sources.title: New 2024 Standing Orders to address Ghana’s dynamic and hybrid parliamentary democracy
sources.summary: Reports Bagbin opened orientation for January 2024 Standing Orders, effective 2 January; notes process changes and committee count from 31 to 44.
sources.relevance: Speaker procedural leadership and remarks.
sources.notes: Full page not separately fetched.

sources.title: Speaker pays a historic visit on the Nayiri
sources.summary: Reports courtesy visit; says Bagbin noted election as CPA President and identified himself as COSAP President; visit part of Fourth Republic anniversary activities.
sources.relevance: Public engagement and international parliamentary roles.
sources.notes: Claims attributed to article.

sources.title: Thirty years of inception of Fourth Republican Parliament
sources.summary: Parliament retrospective states Fourth Republic Parliament began 7 January 1993 and identifies Bagbin as current Speaker in 2023.
sources.relevance: Career-start institutional context.
sources.notes: Institutional account, not an individual member biography.

sources.title: Remarks by incoming Majority Leader
sources.summary: Ayariga said Bagbin had risen from Minority Leader to Majority Leader, served in the Executive, risen from Deputy Speaker, and become Speaker.
sources.relevance: Attributed record of previous leadership roles.
sources.notes: Statement is by Ayariga and supplies no dates for Bagbin’s prior roles.

sources.title: Speaker clarifies Matthew Nyindam still remains MP for now
sources.summary: Reports Speaker’s view that Nyindam retained membership during a seven-day stay period after High Court election ruling and gives his reasoning.
sources.relevance: Speaker’s interpretation and communication.
sources.notes: Do not treat attributed legal view as an independent legal conclusion.

sources.title: No anti-media laws under my watch — Bagbin assures journalists
sources.summary: Reports an assurance against laws stifling journalists, delivered by MP Rita Naa Odoley Sowah on Bagbin’s behalf; says he has been in Chamber since 1993.
sources.relevance: Public position and parliamentary-career beginning.
sources.notes: Speech was read on his behalf, not personally delivered at event.

sources.title: Speaker donates to Ghana National Fire Service, Nadowli Kaleo Students Union and Sombo SHS
sources.summary: Reports donations, including GH¢100,000 for fire-service fence completion and support for student union and school.
sources.relevance: Documented activity in the Upper West/Nadowli-Kaleo area.
sources.notes: Does not establish constituency or election result.

sources.title: Speaker commissions ICT lab in Kaleo
sources.summary: Reports inauguration of Yamoransa Model ICT/STEM centre in Kaleo and Bagbin’s call for community ownership.
sources.relevance: Documented public engagement and activity.
sources.notes: No constituency history inferred.

sources.title: Parliament news archive listing
sources.summary: Archive includes links to numerous Bagbin-related items, including 2026 reports and 2023 retrospective.
sources.relevance: Discovery route for dated Speaker news and activities.
sources.notes: Long fetched output truncated by tool; key news items separately inventoried.

sources.title: Report of the Committee on Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs on the Plant Breeder’s Bill
persons: Committee on Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs
sources.locator: Repository item metadata; date and author fields
sources.summary: Repository metadata dates the item 2013-11, names Bagbin as author, and links a 673.14 KB committee report PDF concerning the Plant Breeder’s Bill.
sources.relevance: Evidence of an authored committee report and legislative scrutiny activity.
sources.notes: PDF not downloaded or examined; metadata does not establish Bagbin’s committee membership, chairmanship, vote, or bill sponsorship.

sources.title: Report of the Committee of the Whole on the Public Elections (Registration of Voters) Regulations, 2023 and other related matters
sources.document_type: Committee of the Whole report / PDF
sources.term_or_session: Seventh and Eighth Parliament Constitutional Instruments collection
sources.locator: Repository item date, author, and collection metadata
sources.summary: Repository dates the report 2023, names Bagbin as author, and links the 2.9 MB Public Elections PDF.
sources.relevance: Evidence of an authored report concerning voter-registration regulations.
sources.notes: PDF not downloaded or examined; metadata establishes author listing, not a specific personal role beyond authorship.

events.description: Parliament says Bagbin had been in the Chamber since the Fourth Republic began in 1993; initial election date and constituency are not established from inspected primary records.
events.notes: Year only; exact date of individual entry is not established.

events.description: Parliament repository catalogues Bagbin’s closing remarks at dissolution of Sixth Parliament.
Indexed text for Parliament-hosted results reports Bagbin as NDC candidate in Nadowli West with 12,997 votes (61.9%).
events.notes: PDF not locally processed; not direct file verification.

events.description: Repository metadata names Bagbin as author of the Committee on Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs report on the Plant Breeder’s Bill.
events.notes: Authorship documented; membership, chairmanship, and individual vote are not established by metadata.

events.description: Incoming Majority Leader described Bagbin as having served as Minority Leader, Majority Leader, in the Executive, and as Deputy Speaker before Speaker.
events.notes: Exact dates and executive portfolio not stated.

events.description: Office of the Speaker history lists Bagbin as Speaker beginning 7 January 2021 and continuing to date.
Repository lists a formal communication authored by Alban S.K. Bagbin as Speaker.
Repository metadata names Bagbin as author of a Committee of the Whole report on Public Elections (Registration of Voters) Regulations, 2023 and related matters.
events.notes: Authorship documented; specific role beyond authorship and report content were not independently established.

events.description: Reported visit to Nayiri; article says Bagbin referred to his CPA and COSAP leadership roles.
New Standing Orders took effect 2 January; orientation opening address reported 17 February.
events.notes: Institutional changes distinguishable from personal legislative acts.

events.description: Ninth Parliament began and parliamentary sources continued to identify Bagbin as Speaker.
Incoming Majority Leader referred to Bagbin’s past roles and experience.
Official page lists a formal communication about happenings at the Appointments Committee.
Speaker intervention at Rabat meeting of Atlantic African countries’ parliamentary Speakers, listed the following day.
Parliament reported Bagbin’s view on MP Matthew Nyindam during stay period following High Court decision.
Parliament reported Bagbin’s assurance about anti-media laws, delivered on his behalf at GJA event.
Remarks on decentralisation, legislative/administrative/oversight responsibility, and Parliament TV.
events.notes: Two pages report similar event with date discrepancy.

events.description: Supreme Court 150th anniversary lecture on the 1992 Constitution, preserved as repository Working Paper.
Ruled a proposed Private Member’s Motion on narcotics seizures inadmissible under specified Standing Orders; article reports reasons concerning ongoing investigations and court proceedings.
